supporting_observations.claim: The repeated HTTPS checks in the alert window went through the explicit proxy to update.chartmate-imaging.com, matching the inventoried ChartMate updater endpoint and its expected roughly five-minute check cadence.
The ChartMate updater was running from its inventoried path, and its process ID is tied to several of those proxy connections by matching process/network records and source ports.
The ChartMate updater process ended shortly after the last observed periodic check.
Separate workstation activity remains unexplained: Explorer recorded a UserAssist entry for mstsc.exe, and the user changed settings related to showing hidden files.
Sysmon recorded svchost.exe accessing LSASS twice. The records do not identify the hosting service or establish that the access was malicious.
Explorer loaded a 7-Zip DLL whose signature status was unavailable; this observation alone does not establish malicious code or execution.
The periodic network activity is well explained by the approved updater, but the separate workstation artifacts are not sufficiently explained to support closing the broader activity as benign.

known_telemetry_limitations: The listed winsec and Sysmon collection outage affects WS-LPARK-01 from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, not WS-BCARTER-01.
The records show LSASS access events but do not identify the specific service hosted by svchost.exe PID 6000.
The supplied records do not show the destination or purpose of the mstsc.exe activity.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish that the ChartMate connections carried malicious content or data exfiltration.
The evidence does not establish whether mstsc.exe connected to a remote system, which system it may have connected to, or whether the activity was authorized.
The evidence does not establish that the LSASS accesses resulted in credential theft.
The evidence does not establish that the 7-Zip DLL or the observed registry changes were malicious or were used for persistence.
additional_evidence_needed: Identify the service and executable hosted by svchost.exe PID 6000 and review its signature, command line, and surrounding process activity.
Collect endpoint or RDP/network telemetry that can determine whether mstsc.exe actually connected to a host and identify the target and logon context.
Verify the 7-Zip DLL's path, hash, publisher, and installation provenance.
Review startup-folder contents and the provenance of the Common Startup registry value to determine whether any startup item was added.
Validate the ChartMate updater binary's signature and hash and, if available, inspect update/package records for the observed checks.
